Oroku Saki (also known as the Shredder) was the deadly and nefarious leader of the and and the ' vengeful arch-nemesis. He takes on the role of one of the main antagonists of the Nickelodeon 2012 TV series.

The Shredder is a slim, but tall, brawny, and toned Japanese man with shiny, chrome plated armor on his chest, shoulders, arms and lower legs, worn over a maroon outfit with a dark blue cape hanging over his back. His signature helmet, the Kuro Kabuto, is perhaps the most notable aspect of his appearance and it covers up his face because it was partially burned and disfigured, such to the extent that he has very little vision left in his right eye.

Unlike previous incarnations of the Shredder who held tekko-kagi in their hands, this version uses customized, partially mechanical ones built into his gauntlets. His armor is also larger and bulkier than previous versions, except perhaps , though it's streamlined and smooth at the same time. The spikes on it are larger, longer and more blade-like than most previous versions (though once again bearing some similarities to Ch'rell's). As previously stated this Shredder suffers a serious, disfiguring burn on the right side of his face; a considerably greater injury than the scratch marks (from Splinter) most others possess that leaves him nearly, or completely, blind in that eye.

He approached and asked him for a favor, requesting that the rescue his chihuahua dog "" from a group of Yakuza who wanted him to throw his next fight for gambling purposes. While Tattoo is engaged in his Sumo match, the TMNT, Ninjara and the Warrior Dragon infiltrate the mob headquarters and rescue the fiesty pup. Tattoo wins his match and the Turtles return Inky to his right owner. The wrestler awards a beloved katana as thanks for saving his dog.

entities.description:
Takeshi, also known as Tiger Claw, is a mutant tiger assassin and bounty hunter who becomes an ally of the and an enemy of the , and the brother of in the 2012 TV series. He perfectly knows his profession, making him an extremely dangerous opponent.

As a human, Takeshi was a young Japanese boy with short straight hair and a thin figure. He wore a tank top with a star graphic on the front, shorts, and crew socks.

Tiger Claw is a mutant tiger with short orange and white fur with black stripes, pink and black skin, yellow eyes, and a large, muscular figure. He has four fingers on each hand and three toes on each foot, black claws, white whiskers on his muzzle, and a docked tail. After losing his right arm to in "Tale of Tiger Claw", he sports a mechanical arm, allowing him to change his hand into a gun, a claw, or a rocket launcher. He wears a cyan shirt with rolled up sleeves, a brown shirt vest, a double chain bullet bandolier with a jetpack, an azure scarf around his neck, a double chain bullet belt around his waist, and brown pants with pouches for his pistols on his thighs and belted bottoms that stop at his ankles. After the events of "The Wrath of Tiger Claw", he wears an eye patch over his left eye and his right ear is slightly damaged.

Given his predatory nature, Tiger Claw is fierce and cunning, finding enjoyment in hunting and outsmarting most of his enemies. As such he shares no qualms in attacking defenseless people, like when refused to harm , seeing no honor in attacking a blind person, even attempting to kill his own sister Alopex. Tiger Claw holds no such code of honor, he cares only for power and revenge. Regardless, he follows the 's orders without question, given their mutual respects.

entities.description:
In the IDW continuity, Tusk is the leader of the , a motorcycle gang of mutant pigs living in Mutant Town, Manhattan. She first appeared along with her gang in Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles #110. She eventually became a member of Jennika's band Created in Darkness.

Soon, Raph and Tusk were both on motorcycles, with Raph on one borrowed from the gang, and Al stood in front to officiate the beginning of their . The race started with the two speeding through a construction site. Raph was initially in the lead, but Tusk soon pulled ahead. As Tusk swerved around a stack of s, Raph decided to ride directly through one of them. Raph thought he was in the lead, but Tusk had ridden up a ramp and flew ahead of him. But her lead was brief, as she suddenly slammed face-first into some building rubble, violently knocking her onto the ground.

Raph decided to stop the race and went over to help the injured Tusk. Raph helped Tusk limp back to the start of the race, telling of Tusk's accident. Tusk decided that Raph was the winner, but Raph insisted that neither of them won. Tusk decided to let Raph keep the motorcycle the Road Hogs had loaned him, and declared Raph and Al were cool with the Road Hogs. Raph and Al rode off together on Raph's new bike.

Tusk later joined in at a support group hosted at Alopex's shelter, also attended by fellow Mutant Towners Bea, , , , , Jo, , , , Sheena, and Wanda. The group debated various topics affecting them all in Mutant Town, but on the extremely polarizing issue of , Tusk defended him. Tusk said that, as a human, she had no one in her life, she was sick, and was an . But since Hob's , she had made friends among other people in the same situation, she had the support group, and she was also motivated to quit drinking. Jay and Mona were irritated by this defense of Hob, as they had all still been mutated against their will, and Hob's were still abusive with their newfound power and were poor managers of the community's resources. The argument in the support group became heated and eventually spiraled out of control, resulting in a short brawl which would only be broken up by the commanding voice of reason of former Mutanimal .

André — sometimes transliterated as Andre — is the French and Portuguese form corresponding to the English name Andrew and is now also used in the English-speaking world. It is used in France, Quebec, Canada and other French-speaking countries, as well as in Portugal, Brazil and other Portuguese-speaking countries. It is a variation of the Greek name Andreas, a short form of any of various compound names derived from andr- 'man, warrior'.

The name is popular in Norway and Sweden.

entities.name: Azokk
entities.description:
In Eastman and Laird's Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles Volume 4, Azokk was a diplomat for the .

Azokk believed that the conflict between the s and the Styracodons should have a peaceful solution, and traveled to the Styracodons to negotiate a treaty. However, he was betrayed and captured, his horns cut off and both his eyes gouged out, and was sent to a Styracodon extrajudicial prison, Royal Detention Center 17, to live out his days.

32 years later, was sent to the same prison, having been captured and smuggled off Earth after a one-night stand with the Styracodon Regenta Seri. Azokk had been in the prison long and had been resigned to his fate, but he soon shepherded and befriended Mikey to his new plight. Azokk finds it remarkable that Mikey continues to hold out hope even after his kidnapping, imprisonment and weeks of torture and starvation.

One day, in the prison courtyard, Mikey and Azokk are together in the courtyard. Mikey sees Seri being escorted by Styracodon bodyguards atop one of the high prison walls. Azokk listens as Mikey daringly scales the walls for a chance to see Seri again, but is overpowered by the guards and knocked back into the courtyard.

entities.name: Blind ninja
entities.description:
The blind ninja is an unnamed who first appeared in Tales of the TMNT volume 2 issue 5: Blind Faith. He is never seen in person, as his very first act is to blind when their fight begins. In the comics, the blind ninja is only ever depicted in a series of stark black and white silhouettes to simulate Leonardo's sightlessness.

Before the events of Blind Faith, this ninja was among the various Foot Ninja that the fought sometime in the past. Leonardo blinded this ninja in battle, though Leo himself can never remember when or where this happened, much less who this ninja was. When the ninja was blinded, his other senses compensated and became sharper, but the Foot Clan retired him from combat and put him to work polishing other ninja's weapons. This indignity motivated the blind ninja to seek revenge against the enemy who maimed him.

In Blind Faith, the blind ninja attacks Leonardo, and the very first thing he does is use drug-tipped to blind the turtle through his bloodstream. Leo is forced to fight his opponent completely blind, but soon realizes his opponent is just as blind as he is. Fighting on a city rooftop, the blind ninja tells the turtle his story. The battle changes course, and Leo manages to impale the blind ninja on his katana. But the turtle is horrified to realize that his victim is not the blind ninja, but a nearby innocent . This had been the blind ninja's revenge—to take the turtle's sight, and then to take the Turtle's honor from him.

In Tales of Leonardo: Blind Sight, Leonardo is still blind weeks after the battle, and struggles to come to terms with the battle's consequences as he experiences a crisis of purpose. The blind ninja's words and actions continue to taunt the Turtle. During a visit to the woods outside Northampton, Leo is revisited by the blind ninja, and is drawn into a fierce forest battle with him, but afterward cannot be certain this experience was not a dream or hallucination. Splinter suggests that his son's blindness may be more psychological than physical, and serves Leonardo his special brew of infini-tea to help him find the answers in his subconscious. In the end, Leo finally realizes he could not remember the homeless man breathing when he killed him—the man was already dead, having already been killed by the blind ninja and placed in front of Leonardo's blade to force the turtle to suffer the psychological trauma of taking an innocent life. With this revelation, Leo's crushing guilt is alleviated, and his sight returns on its own.

entities.description:
Bludgeon is a mutant hammerhead shark created by the .

He was mutated sometime prior to the events of the New Mutant Order arc. During Shredder's meeting in the Atlantic Ocean with Krang, he and Koya were used as the Foot Clan's contingency plan, in the event that the negotiations became dangerous. When Krang turned on Shredder, Bludgeon and Koya successfully attacked Krang's forces before spiriting their master off the sinking ship.

Along with Koya, Bludgeon was involved with the attempted invasion of Burnow Island. Though they attempted to defend Shredder to the end, they were both driven from the island by the terraformed atmosphere.

After Shredder's return, Bludgeon was involved in the Gauntlet between Shredder and Splinter, in which he was one of the four mutants who fought against the Turtles. He was defeated by Donatello when the mechanized Turtle (who was in an android body at the time) blasted an incredibly bright light in his eyes, blinding him. He attempted to save Koya when Leonardo slashed off her flight feathers, but the two were left permanently crippled.

entities.description:
In the , Blind Buck is the name of a blind human homeless man who was 's first friend after mutating. Shortly after becoming a mutant turtle, a panicked Raphael accidentally crashed into Buck's shopping cart. Buck gave Raphael a blanket and some food, and later gave the Turtle the gray hoodie he would wear until he was found by .

Soon after, Buck and Raphael encountered a trio of street thugs, who struck Buck hard enough to fatally wound him. Raphael was enraged and attacked the criminals for hurting his friend, then held the dying Buck until he passed away. After his loss, Raph was alone again until he encountered during the events of Change is Constant, part 1.

Though Buck only knew Raphael briefly, his kindness and friendship made a great impression on the Turtle, and his loss was very painful.

Fu Lun first appeared in Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles Guide to the Universe, a supplement of Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles & Other Strangeness.

Fu Lun is basically a cheerful man who is accepting of the way things are. He has a karmic view of the universe.

For Fu Lun, the blind monk, the religious heritage of his people is of the utmost importance. He is extremely devout. Through the years, the temple has been threatened by enemies, so this is not the first time. Fu Lun sees this as yet another attempt at a purge. He has already encountered aliens and since he knows nothing of the spaceship, he mistakes these aliens for "Yeti".

Hattori Tatsu was the former sensei of and the main antagonist of the episode "The Forgotten Swordsman."

Hattori Tatsu is a masked swordsman who was the right-hand man of the and mostly operated in Japan. While Tatsu was born blind, he had talents that were discovered by Shredder who brought him into the . He was also a trainer of . Sometime after the death of Super-Shredder, Karai made an attempt on Tatsu's life but failed. Since then, Tatsu began to recruit some that left Karai's side when they started to doubt her leadership, and desired to obtain the in order take control of the Foot Clan entirely.

After defeating Karai and in the first battle, Tatsu knocked aside and encountered a revived who offered him to help bring the Foot Clan back together, which made Rahzar question his own loyalty to Shredder. When it came to the fight at one of the Foot Clan's safe-houses, Karai and Shinigami were assisted by the , , and . Even though Karai knocked off his oni mask where his backstory was explored, Tatsu managed to badly defeat Casey Jones and Shinigami. With help from the Turtles using Casey Jones' explosive pucks, Karai was able to throw off Tatsu's senses and defeat him. Rahzar showed up with and . As the Kuro Kabuto was claimed, Kavaxas drained Tatsu of his soul and then destroyed the Foot Clan safe-house. It is heavily implied that he is burned into ashes from off-screen after Kavaxas fires from his fire breathing mouth.

Tatsu's spirit would later appear in End Times after Kavaxas was free of Tiger Claw’s control, but ended up getting sent back into the Netherworld by April, , and .

entities.description:
Mrs. Morrison is an old, blind woman, that appears only in "". She befriends , after mistaking him for someone sent by Mr. Rosetti.

In the aftermath of the invasion, many of New York City's residents wary of aliens. Taking a shortcut during a race with , drops down to the streets and is seen by a mob. Thinking him an alien, they give chase. Trying to stay away from them, Raph inadvertently runs down a dead-end alley. Just before the mob turns down the same alley a door opens, and an elderly woman steps out. The woman, named Mrs. Morrison is blind. She calls out to ask who's there and Raphael answers with his name. Mrs. Morrison thinks he's the boy sent by Mr. Rosetti to help her move and invites Raph inside. He's reluctant but hears the mob growing close and goes into the apartment. When the mob reaches the alley, they ask if she's seen any aliens. Mrs. Morrison laughs and says no. Once Raph is inside the old lady's apartment, he helps her move some large boxes. Raphael learns that she is being forced out of her home by the bank, as she has run out of money since her husband passed away. All she has is her cat, . After the boxes are moved around, Raph sits down to tea with Mrs. Morrison. Lucy the cat takes a shine to the Turtle and Mrs. Morrison says the cat doesn't like many people.

When Raph prepares to leave, Mrs. Morrison invites him to come again some time. Having already developed a fondness for the woman, Raph is touched by the invitation. Raph gets back to the lair just before and return from their adventure. When Mikey displays the briefcase filled with money that he took from , it gives Raph an idea. Later, he returns to Mrs. Morrison's apartment with the briefcase. Raph knocks on the door and when the kindly old lady answers the door, the ninja hands her the briefcase filled with cash. He tells her that someone left it on her doorstep, and that she has a guardian angel who wants her to stay right where she belongs.

Raphael has just had a running battle with a group of , but after defeating them, he discovers that dozens more are looking for him. Tired, he ducks into an alley to evade them. He leans against a door in the alley, but it is suddenly opened by an elderly woman. Raphael shrinks back, ready for her to scream and freak out, but she does neither. He quickly discovers that she is blind.

The woman, Mrs. Morrison, invites Raphael inside because she assumes he was sent by Mr. Rossetti. There are numerous boxes in her apartment and she needs help moving them into the cellar. As Raphael moves the boxes, he is watched by Mrs. Morrison's pet cat, .

Once the boxes are moved, Mrs. Morrison serves Raphael a cup of tea. As he drinks his tea, Lucy winds her way around his neck, meowing and purring in his ear. Mrs. Morrison tells Raphael that Lucy used to live in the alley out back and they adopted each other. She says that Lucy doesn't usually get along with strangers. Raphael posits that Lucy likes him because he's a bit of an alley cat, too.

entities.description:
Mr. Murakami, also called Murakami-san, is an elderly blind man who owns and operates a noodle shop. He is a character in the 2012 TV series and first appears in "Never Say Xever".

Murakami is a skillful Japanese ramen chef, who runs a ramen shop called 24/7. His restaurant operates through a traditional Japanese-inspired process, with customers putting their orders through a token machine and giving Murakami the token with their corresponding order - even though he is blind, he is able to feel the token's engraving and determine what the customer wants. He becomes a friend to the after they save him from an extortion attempt by the . Despite being blind, he knows what the Ninja Turtles are, but accepts them for who they are (mostly because they saved his life more than once).

After they save him from the Purple Dragons, Murakami rewards the Turtles with a dish called "pizza gyōza" (a type of Japanese-style dumpling that is stuffed with pizza ingredients) which the Ninja Turtles love. When the Turtles attempt to flee from the , holds Murakami hostage to force the Turtles to stay. While Xever is able to outmatch all four Turtles, they are able to hold him off with a water tower and save Mr. Murakami, who happily gives them more pizza gyōza.

In "Karai's Vendetta", and go to his restaurant. Because April had never seen her face to face and Murakami had not heard of her, they are unaware that Karai is an enemy, and April actually befriends her. Murakami knows something is wrong when her tile reads suppon nabe, also known as Turtle Soup. After Karai tries (and enjoys) April's pizza gyōza, the latter is about to try some of the soup, until she learns of its nature. She tries to leave, but is unable to escape the much more skilled ninja. Murakami then buys April some time by throwing the turtle soup in Karai's face and blocking her path. Despite his efforts, Karai then corners April and beats her up, yet April is able to escape.

He snuck into Leonardo's room as the latter was reading, and climbed up the wall and clung to the ceiling. Leo was startled when he realized the octopus was above him.

Stone pounced on Leo, and they briefly fought in Leo's room. But Stone soon squirted Leo with octopus ink and started escaping. Leo followed in hot pursuit across the rooftops of Mutant Town, unknowingly followed by the weasels. Leo tracked Stone to the new , where Leo infiltrated with a combination of disguises and by pretending to be a new recruit. Inside, Leo overheard Stone and talking about how Hob was convinced that the Splinter Dōjō was being set up as an armed stronghold to rival the Mutanimals' power in Mutant Town, and how the Mutanimals would keep investigating the building until they could uncover any secret plans. But the eavesdropping was interrupted when Zanna, missing her father, ran out into view to reunite with Hob. Leo threw a shuriken at the room's overhead light fixture, darkening the room, and swiftly grabbed all three weasels and fled. Leo and the weasels started heading back to the Dōjō to warn the Splinter Clan of the new threat.

entities.name: Varlesh
entities.description:
The Varlesh are a shy, peaceful -like species of giant crustaceans mostly found in the forested areas the Planet D'Hoonib. After more than two million years of mutagenic activity, they have finally settled into their current and somewhat sedentary state. Somewhat hive minded, when intruders invade any particular enclave of Varlesh, these aliens will simultaneously hide within their shells seeming to be just "part of the facade" and landscape. Or at least appearing as merely docile, non-threatening shells. Exclusivity and scarcity of the crab-creatures works to their advantage. Many would-be enemies on D'Hoonib and their scientists are unfamiliar with the species, thus are oblivious to the camouflage and hiding tactics of the Varlesh. This allows them to continue living in a relative peace. They rely on psionics, psychic communication for general information gathering, passing, and amusement. They can sense sentient beings all at once both of ally and hostile intent. As younglings, they will wander the galaxy mixing with other alien species. Once in their adult form they usually settle down on planets or portions of planets of heavy vegetation. Their older, slightly more sedate nature allows vegetation to also grow on their shells. This allows them to blend in even more among particularly forested environs. While the Varlesh are small in numbers, one currently nameless representative crustacean became an unexpected ally, friend, and voice of reason to the Fugitoid. Though it's the only one who is seen speaking aloud, it speaks for the Varlesh community in the Forest as a whole.

Shortly after the Fugitoid's famous mind-melding accident, General Blanque of the Federation sends his men to destroy the "Killer Robot" after landing at Honeycutt's lab near the wooded areas of D'Hoonib. The General was down to make his demands on Honeycutt for the information on the Transmat, so that he may use it as a deadly military weapon. Discovering the humanoid Honeycutt's charred remains was when he ordered his Federats to open fire on what he thought was merely the good doctor's old robot assistant, SAL. Fugitoid tried to alert the soldiers that he was indeed Honeycutt, but they wouldn't listen. As they continued to reign fire on the Robot, he fled for the forest. After Blanque uncovered the Professor's recordings of the accident, he was thrilled as Robots had no rights in this portion of the galaxy. This would make his pursuit of the Fugitoid to obtain his knowledge of the Transmat even easier. Or so he thought. He ordered his men to search the woods for the android.

Honeycutt eventually came to a dense portion of the forest and a small clearing of Varlesh shells. The moss, lichen, and fungi on the shells made them look rather old. Fugitoid had hoped to hide amongst them to throw off the duo of Federats on his trail.

entities.description:
Aevyon is an adolescent school age alien child who appears in the Mirage continuity. Aevyon is an inquisitive boy.

Professor Obligado visits a classroom of diverse alien schoolchildren who are allowed to ask him questions. One student, Aevyon, asks the professor what happens if someone falls off the universe. The teacher, Ms. Grundi, scolds Aevyon for asking such a silly question and wants the child to ask something more sensible. However, Obligado is intrigued; he does not know the answer, but intends to find out for himself. After a fact finding mission that takes him places both physical, mental, and spiritual, Obligado returns to the classroom. He asks if Aevyon remembers the question he posed the last time the Professor spoke to them. Aevyon does, and repeats the question. Obligado apologizes and admits that he does not know. Aevyon finds it scary that there are things even the most advanced science still cannot answer. Obligado agrees.

Aka was murdered by her own sister Kitsune in Shredder in Hell issue #5, to provide a sacrifice of divine blood to resurrect the Dragon. She later was resurrected, after gathering information warned to warn Kitsune and Oroku Saki about the Rat King's Armageddon Game.

Aka expressed herself as a kind old woman. As the eldest surviving member of the Pantheon, she took her position seriously and loved all her siblings as family.

But unlike most of the Pantheon, Aka also loved and respected humans, considering them to be the Pantheon's true children, and wanted to give humanity a fair chance of succeeding on its own merits. To this end, Aka had befriended and supernaturally aided , a human woman. However, Aka was clear that this fairness she sought for humanity was not a guarantee of their success but merely honoring their right to pursue their own destiny without unfair sabotage, accepting that humanity may still yet die out as a result of their own failures.

entities.name: Bailey
entities.description:
Bailey is a character appearing in the series. She is a member of the improvisational troupe at Eastman High and one of 's friends.

One day at Eastman High, and his friends Bailey and are honing their improv skills. When Mikey asks them for prompts, both call out that they want him to do something with mutants. An annoyed Mikey says that all they want is to hear cool mutant stories. Madison complains that they've been hanging out for months and he's never told them any of the cool mutant stuff he does. Bailey says that he has to have some stories. Mikey gives in and promises to tell them a story involving danger, mystery, friendship, betrayal and lots of improve. Both of his friends are excited. The story unfolds with Mikey's other friend, Rod Underwood, Jr., constantly sending people to kidnap the for their blood. After another failed attempt, Mikey's brothers tell him to dump Rod as a friend. Mikey doesn't want to do this, and is still thinking about it when he's supposed to be mirroring during improv practice. Bailey has to call his name several times to snap him out of it. Mikey asks if they ever have a thing where they have a friend but their other friends don't like him. Madison asks if this is about Rod and Bailey wants to know how Mikey is even friends with the guy. She says that he's always coming to the school and messing up their rehearsals. Madison mimics Rod, talking about his various demands and Bailey adds that Rod doesn't smell great either. Rod is suddenly there and explains his BO. The lack of enthusiasm at his appearance makes him storm out, but only after stating he's going live tonight on all socials. After he's gone, Mikey asks Bailey and Madison what time it is and both groan in frustration.

After Rod is kidnapped, Mikey tries to get his brothers to help find him. They won't, so later at the school, Mikey is pacing and complaining how nobody cares. Madison tells him this is not specific for their scene work. Bailey sighs in exasperation and says his brothers might be right and Madison agrees. Bailey adds that Rod is kind of awful. Madison says that obviously being kidnapped is a terrible thing, but everyone sort of... hates Rod. This gives Mikey an idea and he realizes that he must have been kidnapped by someone who hates him the most. He doesn't notice the looks his friends exchange. Bailey asks who that would be and Mikey decides they have to start with Bishop. He talks them both into coming with him, but they are all almost attacked by . Bishop calls off the Mechazoids, so Mikey and his friends sit down to ask about Rod. Unfortunately, Mikey sneezes and the Mechazoids think he's attacking. As they battle Mikey, another Mechazoid pushes Bailey and Madison into the elevator so they can leave.

entities.description:
William "Will" Byers is a main character in Stranger Things. Will is the foster brother of Eleven.

The kids from Hawkins arrive in New York City as tourists and are soon joined by Eleven, who took a bus by herself in order to join her friends. When they are waiting for a subway train, they hear a noise that sounds familiar and follow the sound into the tunnels. They soon encounter a group of giant demodogs but before they can attack the kids, the Turtles appear and destroy the creatures. Afterwards, the two groups retire to the where introductions and explanations are made. In answer to a question from , Will explains that the Demogorgons come from the Upside Down, but they can cross over.

Will, along with Mikey, Michael, and Lucas, locate a subway train sitting on a secluded track far back in the tunnels which seems to be the source of the spores. Demogorgons enter the car they are in and attack, taking down Leo and Mikey. Will and his two friends scoop up the Turtles' weapons and stand ready to do battle.

Back in the subway car, Mike, Lucas and Will are slashing away at the vines spilling from the open gate while Leonardo and Michelangelo continue fighting Demogorgons. Will stops when he spots something at the feet of a passenger and finds a lighter. Mike calls out that they need help and Will proceeds to wrap cut vines around one of Leo’s katana, stating that he’s found a way to speed things up. Leo approaches him and asks if the creatures don’t like fire, to which Will responds that they hate it. Taking the sword, Leo says they’ll put that to the test and Will sets the sword on fire. Leo slices through the gateway and he and his group enter the Upside Down. Lucas says he hoped never to see what it was like and Mike checks that Will is okay. The groups steps out onto the subway platform and sees people piled on top of each other on the stair. Leonardo is examining one of the prone humans and Mike asks what he’s thinking. Leo says that they might be in for more surprises as he opens the man’s shirt to reveal an . Leo tells the boys that Utroms are alien beings hiding on Earth, but that they thought they were all gone. Mikey says that the one they just found looks a little sick and he’s never seen one with veins like it has. Will immediately flicks open a lighter and sets fire to the Utrom. Leo jumps forward and demands to know what Will is doing. Will replies that he’s saving it. A smokey substance comes out of the Utrom and drifts up the stairs. Leo asks where it’s going and Will tells him that it’s rejoining the rest of The Mind Flayer, their enemy – wherever he’s hiding. The last panel shows The Mind Flayer perched atop a tall building.

entities.description:
Chang Lao is a young man recently arrived in New York City from China in the Mirage Continuity.

A young Chinese boy named Chang Lao is being chased through the streets of New York City by a group of bullies. As he tries to hide from them, he wishes he could go home to China. There, in his small village, life was simple. Here, he and his family do not fit in. They left China to escape religious persecution and found freedom in America. However, they also found more hate and violence than they thought possible.

When he is spotted, Chang Lao tries to climb a fire escape ladder, but is caught. The head bully is after him because Chang Lao did not make his protection payment. On night maneuvers close by, hears the commotion and sees what is happening. He steps in to chase the bullies away and then explains to Chang Lao that he is a ninja, not a demon. Don leaves when the boy's father calls him to come upstairs. However, Don goes to listen at their apartment window and hears the father tells his son that their way is that of non-violence, which is why Chang Lao did not fight back.

Don takes to following the boy to and from school. The bullies once more spot Chang Lao and start chasing him. Chang Lao is cornered and a bully cuts him with a switchblade seconds before Don arrives. The begins pounding the bullies and then one of them pulls a gun. entities.description:
Cookie, along with and appear in River Hymn. They are three young boys, all friends, who live in Booders Falls.

Three young boys take their fishing rods down to the polluted river that runs through the town of Booders Falls. One of the boys, , asks if it's safe to fish there, and tells him it is, as long a Officer Mannigan doesn't catch them. Owen comments on the smell and guesses the river is polluted and that's why the cops always chase them away. Cookie says that the cops don't want them down there because they're afraid the ghosts will get them. Owen is concerned about a ghost, but Ray says that Cookie is just pulling his leg. Cookie offers proof and Ray threatens him if he's pulling a gag. Owen, however, is honestly scared. Cookie says he should be because the ghost is real. He pulls aside some vines and shows his friends some carvings on the rocks. Owen thought they were supposed to be carvings from the old, old days, but Cookie says that doesn't explain why new ones are always showing up. Fresh carvings, he says, ones that weren't there before. Ray points out more carvings a little farther away and as they make their way over, Owen asks how Cookie knows it's a ghost. Cookie replies that these were sacred Indian burial grounds and their ghosts aren't happy will all the factories that were built here. As they examine another set of carvings, Cookie says his father told him the whole area was peppered with them at one time, but they were covered up when the canals, dams, and factories were built. Ray draws their attention to a fresh carving of a turtle and then the boys hear the motor of an approaching boat.

Peering around the rocks, they see that it isn't Mannigan approaching, but a game warden. Ray wants to run for it, but Owen has left his father's fishing pole near the water and wants to get it. Ray is sure they'll be busted because they don't have fishing licenses, but Cookie urges them to shut up because the warden is coming their way. The trio wait, thinking that the warden is passing by, but then he comes up behind them to ask what they are doing there. However, it's not a game warden, it's Bloodsucker. He grabs Cookie and says that he is going to eat him. Cookie yells for his friends to help as Bloodsucker carries him towards a cave. Owen looks for his dad's fishing rod, but Ray says they have to do something. Ray agrees, and finding the pole, casts the line at Bloodsucker, hooking his pant's leg. This causes Bloodsucker to fall and lose his hold on Cookie. The three boys start running, but Bloodsucker pops up behind a tree, announcing that he'll enjoy feasting upon their blood.

To stop Casey's beating, the Turtles begin throwing trash can lids at the gang. The interruption lasts long enough for Danny's mom to call him in for dinner, which breaks up the attack. It is then that the Turtle tots decide to teach young Casey self-defense.

The Turtles were not altogether successful in teaching young Casey any self-defense techniques, but he did learn from them to stand up for himself and his friend. When Casey saw the bullies picking on Stevie and stealing his books, he becomes so angry that he attacks Danny McDonough and takes him down. Grabbing a hockey stick from one of the bullies, Casey defeats and chases off the rest of the group. Upon accessing the Episode's third section, Slashuur reveals that this land is the Turtle's Future, one potential future should things continue as they are. The Turtles defeat Slashuur once more and have a conversation with him, which helps him remember his missing memories. After clearing the third section of the Unknown City, the name "Future" is permanently shown in both the area map (replacing "Unknown City") and in the Station Warp (replacing ??????????).

The Station Warp area is generally in the same position as the Turtle's home. The first area is a Subway tunnel while the second area is the streets with signs saying 8 Main Street and Down Town. The Clear Result screen is a ruined variation of New York's Clear Result screen.

Notably, the Future houses only enemies coming from the , which also marks the first appearance of the Foot Sumo Ninja, one of the strongest enemies in the game. It is hinted that the Foot were responsible for New York's destruction, though the exact nature of the Future's creation remains unclear, with Slashuur simply stating "A battle. Meaningless battles such as this have existed from the distant past and last far into the future".

entities.description:
s afterlife is the place where his soul went before he was resurrected by his descendant . It resembles an endless grassy plain, with a deep river or sea on one side, and a red or blue sky overhead. There is only one structure seen in this entire world: a medieval Japanese castle set on a rocky mountain, where the king of the afterlife dwelt. This location appears in the special Shredder issue of the second Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles Micro-Series by IDW Publishing.

It is unclear precisely what kind of afterlife this is. Saki described it as being the destination for all those who die, and their uniform fate to become shadows of their former selves, without purpose or autonomy. However, and 's near-death experience seem to indicate that this may not necessarily be the case, and that his destination was only one possible place that dead souls might go.

The Saki meets tells him that time works in a special way in the afterlife, explaining how the king Saki slays turns out to be an older version of himself who had been sent back to the afterlife after his ultimate future death.

When Saki tells Kitsune about this afterlife, she claims not to have known Saki would experience an afterlife before being resurrected. She suggests that it is not a real place, but merely a dream containing a lesson Saki was trying to teach himself. Saki concedes the possibility that this may be true, but does not tell Kitsune that he actually experiences this afterlife every time he sleeps, and often even when he just briefly closes his eyes—the vision is always present just beneath the surface of his conscious awareness.

The Esoteric Order of Dagon is a cult which appears in the Eastman and Laird's Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles issue Men of Shadow. They are lead by a group of vampires, headed by Master Traquer, but the bulk of the cultists are people with vaguely fish-like appearances.

As implied by their name, they worship the literal Lovecraftian entity Dagon, and seek to summon it from the waters of Innsmouth, Massachusetts.

The cross the Order when they capture and and tie them up in the Whatley House, setting up a bomb in order to blow them and the house up so they can erase all evidence of their existence from humankind after they become surrounded by SWAT. The Turtles snuck into the house at the same time that Clark Ashton Allard appeared inside. The Turtles offered to just take April and Casey with them and get out of their hair, but Lord Mallet, the highest-ranking in the house at the time, says he'll just blow them all up in there. Clark takes out Mallet and tells the Turtles they need to decapitate the vampires or pierce their hearts with wood if they want to help. The Turtles untie April and Casey, and the leadership of the Order escapes. Allard leapt out the window high into the air with the neo-dead slave holding the bomb and tosses him, allowing the bomb to detonate without any real casualties, although it blew Clark flying.

After Clark was blasted into a field in Arkham, Massachusetts and placed into his "auto-doc" by Maximillian Jones and Pervis Walker, Traquer and some other vampires captured Max and Clark and took them to a Innsmouth Seafood warehouse in Innsmouth, Massachusetts. Just as The Turtles, Casey, and approached on the , the cultists succeeded in summoning Dagon. Dagon grabbed the Turtlebot with one of its tongues and began drawing it into its maw, forcing to eject. Meanwhile, Casey fought Traquer and broke a baseball bat while hitting him. Traquer grabbed Casey to kill him in retaliation, but Max grabbed the broken piece of bat and stabbed Traquer to death with it.

entities.name: Underworld
entities.description:
The underworld, also known as the netherworld or hell, is the supernatural world of the dead in various religious traditions and myths, located below the world of the living. Chthonic is the technical adjective for things of the underworld.

The concept of an underworld is found in almost every civilization and "may be as old as humanity itself". Common features of underworld myths are accounts of living people making journeys to the underworld, often for some heroic purpose. Other myths reinforce traditions that the entrance of souls to the underworld requires a proper observation of ceremony, such as the ancient Greek story of the recently dead Patroclus haunting Achilles until his body could be properly buried for this purpose. People with high social status were dressed and equipped in order to better navigate the underworld.

A number of mythologies incorporate the concept of the soul of the deceased making its own journey to the underworld, with the dead needing to be taken across a defining obstacle such as a lake or a river to reach this destination. Imagery of such journeys can be found in both ancient and modern art. The descent to the underworld has been described as "the single most important myth for Modernist authors".
